title: SIGEM: A Simple yet Effective Similarity based Graph Embedding Method

problem.claim: Graph embedding methods have drawbacks including limited global-structure modeling, reduced learning quality, impaired directed-graph degree distributions, and limited applicability.

gap.claim: Existing methods do not adequately address these structural, quality, directed-graph, and applicability limitations.

contributions.claim: LINOW is a recursive link-based graph similarity measure using node weights and applicable to directed and undirected graphs.
A non-approximate matrix formulation and single-node and batch-node variants are provided to accelerate and scale LINOW computation.
SIGEM is a self-supervised, contrastive-free similarity-based graph embedding method that ranks nodes using LINOW-bn and preserves those ranks in embedding vectors with a single-layer neural network.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across eight real-world datasets, LINOW-sn and LINOW-bn reportedly improve the scalability of naive LINOW.
The authors report that LINOW benefits similarity-based graph embedding.

SIGEM reportedly achieves the highest accuracy for graph reconstruction and node classification, and significantly outperforms other methods in most link-prediction cases, compared with thirteen state-of-the-art and conventional embedding methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph embedding methods are established but have four stated drawbacks.
LINOW is introduced as a directed- and undirected-graph similarity measure based on recursive link similarity and node weights.
A matrix formulation and single-node and batch-node variants are introduced to accelerate and scale LINOW.
SIGEM uses LINOW-bn to rank nodes and preserves their original ranks in embedding vectors through a single-layer neural network.
Experiments compare the methods on eight real-world datasets and three task types against thirteen baselines.

source_observation.claim: The method computes similarity-based node rankings and preserves those rankings in the embedding space.

interpretation.claim: Explicitly retaining a structural ordering may provide a simple self-supervised signal for graph embeddings.

application.claim: For graph representation tasks where node similarity or rank is meaningful, consider embedding objectives that preserve similarity-derived rankings.

exception.claim: The reported link-prediction advantage occurs in most cases rather than all cases.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the eight datasets.
The abstract does not specify evaluation metrics or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe LINOW's recursive equations or the matrix formulation.
The abstract does not report computational costs, scalability thresholds, or ablations.
The abstract does not specify the thirteen comparison methods by name.
